recognize_zh: 上圖黑箭頭為漿細胞：偏心核、深藍色胞質；下圖灰箭頭為 Mott 細胞，胞質塞滿大小一致的淡藍色圓形 Russell 小體，像一串葡萄，核被擠到一側。
features: Plasma cell (top, black arrow): small eccentric nucleus with clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Mott cell (bottom, gray arrow): cytoplasm distended by numerous uniform, round, pale blue globules (Russell bodies) in a grape-cluster arrangement
Mott cell nucleus small, dense and compressed to the periphery
Top field also contains two larger cells with fine azurophilic cytoplasmic granules; bottom field contains mononuclear leukocytes
Red cells stacked in rouleaux-like chains in the bottom field
describe_en: Composite of two smear fields. The upper field shows a plasma cell (black arrow) with an eccentric nucleus, clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm, adjacent to two larger cells with fine azurophilic granules. The lower field shows a Mott cell (gray arrow) whose cytoplasm is distended by numerous uniform, round, pale blue Russell bodies, producing a grape-cluster appearance and compressing the nucleus to the periphery; red cells in this field show rouleaux-like stacking, which may reflect hypergammaglobulinemia or a thicker smear area. Mott cells represent immunoglobulin accumulating in dilated endoplasmic reticulum and occur in reactive plasmacytosis (such as HIV infection) as well as plasma cell neoplasms, so they do not by themselves indicate clonality. Findings are consistent with a plasma cell and a Mott cell.

ddx.vs: Dutcher bodies are single pale intranuclear pseudoinclusions overlying the nucleus, not multiple cytoplasmic globules.

ddx.dx: Vacuolated cell (e.g., Burkitt cell or activated monocyte)
ddx.vs: Vacuoles are empty clear holes, whereas Russell bodies are filled, homogeneous pale blue to pink globules.
Crystalline inclusions are angular rods or needles rather than uniform round globules.
